correctness.rationale: Expanding Q_A=v^TAv for v=otimes_j s^(j), independent factor Rademacher signs, shows Q_A-tr A=sum_{nonempty pair patterns P}c_P chi_P. Distinct chi_P are orthogonal Walsh characters, so Var Q_A=sum c_P^2. Pattern groups G_P partition upper-triangular off-diagonal entries and are nonempty, hence all coefficient constraints independent and kernel codimension prod_j(1+binom(d_j,2))-1; g_P=2^(|J(P)|-1)prod_inactive d_j. Orthogonal projection on each group mean-zero hyperplane with symmetric Frobenius doubling yields dist_F(A,K)^2=(1/2)sum c_P^2/g_P; sharp bounds follow. For two factors gmin=2,gmax=max(m,n), so constants 4 and 2max(m,n). SPD witness I4+tK_{+-} has tensor variance 0 or 16t² and ordinary independent-sign variance 8t². Independently enumerated all sign assignments for random symmetric integer matrices in dimensions (2,2),(2,3),(2,2,2), directly verifying variances 96,316,296 and coefficient-count/kernel dimensions. General proof rests on Walsh orthogonality, not these examples. Degenerate D=1 handled separately.
